structured_output.what_is_happening: GoCollect (gocollect.fun) is a real location-based game. Players walk to crates and pull graded cards from Collector Crypt ($CARDS), and it has an X account, @gocollectfun. At least 10 Solana tokens called 'GoCollect / COLLECT' were launched on 2026-09-25. This one (Jdv79…) does not end in 'pump' and its launchpad is unknown. It was put straight into a PumpSwap pool with ~$218k of liquidity, which is more than its $150k market cap. The LP is 0% locked and RugCheck says only a few wallets provide liquidity. The trading looks faked: 1,860 unique buyers but only 54 unique sellers made ~3,800 sells, which points to wash trading or volume bots. GMGN flags 49 bundler wallets holding ~22% of top-trader share. Other copies are much bigger: 2MFqe…pump sits at ~$23M market cap and nDZkn…pump (the earliest, ~$1.6M) matches the ~$1.1M pump.fun figure in search snippets. Several other copies already have zero liquidity.

narrative.description: A real-world-asset / Collector Crypt ecosystem game ('Pokemon Go for graded cards') with a working site and an X account that reports usage numbers (542 players, $82k spent).
narrative.why_spreading: A real product tied to the Collector Crypt/$CARDS ecosystem, launched today. Several same-name tokens are being deployed to catch the attention.

token_connection.why_this_token: Nothing links the project to this contract. It has no pump suffix, no DexScreener profile, and the project website shows no contract address. The only link is the copied name, description and X handle.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 2MFqe3…pump (~$23M market cap, $431k liquidity), nDZkn…pump (~$1.65M, the earliest), 14Gi2… ($1.5M, no volume), and several dead copies with zero liquidity.

authenticity.evidence: 54 unique sellers against 1,860 buyers across ~3,800 sells, $6.2M of volume on a $150k market cap (27x turnover in one hour), 49 bundler wallets, liquidity larger than market cap from what appears to be a single provider, unlocked LP, and GMGN counts 79 tokens tied to the dev's X account (the project's name has been reused over and over).
authenticity.uncertainty: I could not read X, so I cannot rule out real buyers confusing this token with the real one.

structural_risks: 0% of the LP is locked, and it may come from a single provider who can pull it at any time
Liquidity is larger than market cap, which fits a fake 'deep pool' setup
Wash or bot volume (54 unique sellers)
Copycat of a project whose other tokens are far larger
Several same-name copies already rugged to zero liquidity today

structured_output.counterargument: The project is real and in the news today, and many buyers mistake one copy for another. The ~1,860 unique buyers could be real people. If the deployer keeps the pool open, confused flow from the $23M token's buzz could push this one up another 2x toward $300k, since it is still going up. The deep liquidity also means small sells barely move the price.
unknowns: Who provided the LP and whether it is the creator
Which contract the official @gocollectfun account endorses (X was inaccessible)
Whether any buyers are real people rather than bots

source_coverage.notes: x.com returned HTTP 402. The project site lists no contract. Searching for the contract addresses returned nothing. Search snippets point to the pump.fun copy as the one the project uses and mention a Streamflow lock of 18M COLLECT, which does not fit this token.

structured_output.thesis: This looks like a copycat with no pump suffix riding the name of a real Collector Crypt game that launched today. Its liquidity is unlocked and larger than its market cap, and its volume is clearly faked by bots (54 sellers). The token people actually mean is elsewhere. The most likely outcome is that the LP gets pulled, not a 2x.
